reading.ours: two units of arithmetic per iteration
reading.floor: one unit of arithmetic per iteration
reading.caveat: NOT A PRICE — an instrument check, and it is printed first because nothing below it means anything until it passes. The true ratio is a little UNDER 2: both sides pay the driving loop once, so the exact expectation is (2u + L) / (u + L) with L the loop and u one unit, which at sixteen dependent steps per unit puts it around 1.9. A reading below 1.5 means this process could not resolve a deliberate doubling, and the runner voids the report rather than printing prices under it.

reading.ours: one unit of arithmetic per iteration
reading.floor: the same body again, over its own copy of the same state
reading.caveat: NOT A PRICE — the noise floor. The two sides are identical code over identical, separately-allocated state, so the true ratio is 1.00 exactly and every departure from it printed here was produced by this machine at this moment. The rule that follows is the one the whole table is read under: NO RATIO CLOSER TO 1.00 THAN THIS GAP IS A READING. It also bounds the per-row noise figure, which is the same idea measured again inside every pair — each pair times its floor twice, once before our side and once after, and prints how far the two disagreed.

reading.ours: channel.effect(rootSlots, [], body) — a new OIMEffect over 8 roots
reading.floor: createLiteralEffect(channel, rootSlots, body) — a literal over 8 roots, subscribed by a shared function
reading.caveat: THE SAME ALGORITHM IN TWO SHAPES. Ours is the shipped `OIMEffect`, a class whose instance carries its state and its methods. The floor is a plain object literal carrying the same fields, plus two shared functions as own properties (`runIfSourcesChanged`, `setPositionInSourceSlot`) because the channel and `OIMSlotOwner.unsubscribeFromSlot` call those on the effect; the rest is module-level functions taking the object. Both subscribe through the same `OIMSlotOwner.subscribeToSlot`, so `isolate` keeps each arm in its own process. Each arm keeps ONE resident effect alive for the whole process, so the hidden-class loss at a full GC (WHY-EACH-ROW.md, churnChain) is excluded and what remains is the cost of the shape itself. The floor skips the shipped constructor's source-computed dedup `Set` branch and its try/catch, neither of which runs for an effect with no source computeds; it does not build `detachedDispose`, which the shipped class leaves undefined until `disposer` is read. One operation is one effect created and subscribed to 8 roots; the disposal of the pass is in `reset`, untimed.
